extracted.intended_audience: employers, workers, legal practitioners, and members of the public (commenters) interested in the FTC's proposed non‑compete rule
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Trade Commission proposed regulation (NPRM) that defines covered terms, declares certain uses and enforcement of non‑compete clauses to be unfair methods of competition, prescribes notice requirements for existing clauses, and sets out exceptions, state‑law interactions, severability, and the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Non-compete clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-compete clause means: (1) A term or condition of employment that prohibits a worker from, penalizes a worker for, or functions to prevent a worker from: (i) seeking or accepting work in the United States with a different person where such work would begin after the conclusion of the employment that includes the term or condition; or (ii) operating a business in the United States after the conclusion of the employment that includes the term or condition. (2) For the purposes of this part 910, term or condition of employment includes, but is not limited to, a contractual term or workplace policy, whether written or oral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is broad—covers written or oral contractual terms and workplace policies; focuses on post‑employment restrictions on seeking work or operating a business within the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Worker
rubrics_metrics.description: Worker means a natural person who works or who previously worked, whether paid or unpaid, without regard to the worker’s title or the worker’s status under any other State or Federal laws, including, but not limited to, whether the worker is an employee, independent contractor, extern, intern, volunteer, apprentice, or a sole proprietor who provides a service to a person. The term worker includes a natural person who works for a franchisee or franchisor, but does not include a franchisee in the context of a franchisee‑franchisor relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule covers a wide range of working arrangements; status labels under other laws do not determine coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Senior executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior executive means a worker who: (1) Was in a policy‑making position; and (2) Received from a person for the employment: (i) Total annual compensation of at least $151,164 in the preceding year; or (ii) Total compensation of at least $151,164 when annualized if the worker was employed during only part of the preceding year; or (iii) Total compensation of at least $151,164 when annualized in the preceding year prior to the worker’s departure if the worker departed from employment prior to the preceding year and the worker is subject to a non‑compete clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior executive status requires both policy‑making role and meeting the specified compensation threshold (with annualization rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Total annual compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Total annual compensation is based on the worker’s earnings over the preceding year. Total annual compensation may include salary, commissions, nondiscretionary bonuses and other nondiscretionary compensation earned during that 52‑week period. Total annual compensation does not include board, lodging and other facilities as defined in 29 CFR 541.606, and does not include payments for medical insurance, payments for life insurance, contributions to retirement plans and the cost of other similar fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what counts and what does not count toward the compensation threshold for senior executive status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Policy‑making authority and policy‑making position
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy‑making authority means final authority to make policy decisions that control significant aspects of a business entity or common enterprise and does not include authority limited to advising or exerting influence or authority limited to a subsidiary only. Policy‑making position means a business entity’s president, chief executive officer or equivalent, any other officer with policy‑making authority, or any other natural person who has policy‑making authority similar to an officer, subject to subsidiary/common enterprise clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that mere advisory roles or authority limited to a subsidiary do not create policy‑making status unless authority covers the common enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Business entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Business entity means a partnership, corporation, association, limited liability company, or other legal entity, or a division or subsidiary thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard definition to identify the types of organizations covered by 'person' invoking non‑compete clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment means work for a person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad, simple definition aligning with the expansive definition of 'worker.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Entering into or enforcing non‑compete clauses (workers other than senior executives)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a worker other than a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person: (i) To enter into or attempt to enter into a non‑compete clause; (ii) To enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause; or (iii) To represent that the worker is subject to a non‑compete clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non‑senior workers the rule wholly forbids entering, enforcing, or representing existence of non‑competes—covering both attempts and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Entering into or enforcing non‑compete clauses (senior executives)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person: (i) To enter into or attempt to enter into a non‑compete clause; (ii) To enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause entered into after the effective date; or (iii) To represent that the senior executive is subject to a non‑compete clause, where the non‑compete clause was entered into after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior executives are treated differently: non‑competes entered after the effective date may not be enforced or represented; entering new non‑competes is barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for existing non‑compete clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: For each existing non‑compete clause that it is an unfair method of competition to enforce or attempt to enforce, the person who entered into the non‑compete clause with the worker must provide clear and conspicuous notice to the worker by the effective date that the worker’s non‑compete clause will not be, and cannot legally be, enforced against the worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires affirmative, timely notice to affected workers for existing clauses that the employer could not legally enforce after the rule's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of notice and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must: (i) Identify the person who entered into the non‑compete clause with the worker; and (ii) Be on paper delivered by hand to the worker, or by mail at the worker’s last known personal street address, or by email at an email address belonging to the worker (including current work email or last known personal email), or by text message at a mobile telephone number belonging to the worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable delivery methods and requires identification of the party that entered the non‑compete; the employer may use work email as one permissible channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to notice: no record of contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person required to provide notice has no record of a street address, email address, or mobile telephone number, such person is exempt from the notice requirement with respect to such worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an exemption where the employer lacks any contact information for the worker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model language and safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule provides model language (Figure 1 to paragraph (b)(4)) that constitutes notice to the worker that the worker’s non‑compete clause cannot legally be enforced and will not be enforced against the worker. A person complies with the notice requirement if the person provides notice pursuant to the model language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the Commission's model language yields safe‑harbor compliance with the notice obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional notice in additional languages and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to providing the notice in English, a person is permitted to provide such notice in a language (or languages) other than English or to include internet links to translations in additional languages. If providing optional notice, a person may use any Commission‑provided translation of the model language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits multilingual notices and use of Commission translations to reach non‑English speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: Bona fide sale of a business
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of part 910 shall not apply to a non‑compete clause that is entered into by a person pursuant to a bona fide sale of a business entity, of the person’s ownership interest in a business entity, or of all or substantially all of a business entity’s operating assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carves out ordinary non‑competes that are part of bona fide business sales from the prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: Existing causes of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of part 910 do not apply where a cause of action related to a non‑compete clause accrued prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves pre‑existing legal claims that accrued before the rule's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: Good‑faith belief the rule is inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not an unfair method of competition to enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause or to make representations about a non‑compete clause where a person has a good‑faith basis to believe that this part 910 is inapplicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a defense where the enforcing party reasonably and in good faith believes the rule does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to State laws and preservation of State authority and private rights of action
rubrics_metrics.description: This part will not be construed to annul, or exempt any person from complying with any State statute, regulation, order, or interpretation applicable to a non‑compete clause, except that this part 910 supersedes such laws to the extent, and only to the extent, that such laws would otherwise permit or authorize a person to engage in conduct that is an unfair method of competition under § 910.2(a) or conflict with the notice requirement in § 910.2(b. Except with respect to laws superseded, no provision shall be construed as altering, limiting, or affecting the authority of a State attorney general or any other regulatory or enforcement agency or entity or the rights of a person to bring a claim or regulatory action arising under any State statute, regulation, order, or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves state enforcement and private litigation rights, while making clear the federal rule supersedes state law only where state law would permit the prohibited conduct or conflict with the federal notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this part 910 is held to be invalid or unenforceable by its terms, or as applied to any person or circumstance, or stayed pending further agency action, the provision shall be construed so as to continue to give the maximum effect to the provision permitted by law and such invalidity shall not affect the application of the provision to other persons or circumstances or the validity or application of other provisions. If any provision or application of this part is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the provision or application shall be severable from this part 910 and shall not affect the remainder thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability clause directing courts to preserve as much of the rule as legally possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: This part 910 is effective 120 days after date of publication of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the timetable for when prohibitions and notice obligations become operative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority: 15 U.S.C. 45 and 46(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the statutory authority under which the Commission promulgates the rule.
